correctness.rationale: Writing A=dI+[[a,b],[c,0]] gives commutation iff three 2x2 minors of vectors (a,b,c) and (a_prime,b_prime,c_prime) vanish. A nonzero vector of valuation s reduces to a primitive direction in P^2(R/pi^(ell-s)) with (q-1)q^(ell-s-1) unit-scalar choices. Each projective direction has q^2 lifts and q^2+q+1 level-one roots, uniformly over all finite chain rings; the wedge-zero condition is ancestor equality at level ell-s-t when s+t<ell. Thus (q,ell) determines the graph, including free scalar fibers. A noncentral valuation-s matrix has centralizer q^(2ell+2s), with q^ell(q^(3(ell-s))-q^(3(ell-s-1))) occurrences. Distinct degrees recover ell and vertex count q^(4ell) recovers q. Independent direct 2x2 modular multiplication found 88 ordered commuting pairs over F2 and 6400 over Z4, matching the formula.
residual_risks: Full-vertex graph only, not conventional noncentral graph, M2 and finite commutative chain rings only

evidence: Hengbin Zhang 2021 DOI:10.3934/math.2021729 — Its explicit class partition and automorphism result applies to Z/p^s, not arbitrary finite chain rings; it is an important prior mechanism.
Mohammadian 2010 DOI:10.1080/00927870902911771 — Field-target result does not directly compare two nonfield chain rings; risk remains.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known broader theories and reductions were treated as possible covering theorems rather than as title matches. Their actual scope and missing step are identified in the primary-source inspections. Zhang 2021 treats the noncentral graph and wreath-product automorphisms over Z/p^s only, and its level-branching lemma is acknowledged. Neither its ring-family restriction nor field-target rigidity of Abdollahi/Mohammadian states graph equivalence between arbitrary chain rings of matching q and ell. The Z4 versus F2[t]/t² nonisomorphic pair illustrates the new scope; a broader unlocated graph classification remains possible.
